reasoning:
I'm working through the edits needed for round 4, focusing on the `arrivals` annotator prompt's initial ordering logic—how pre-existing cubes are sequenced by oracle pick order versus never-picked ones by distance to bin, and how this affects predictability on the policy side.

The policy's proposed heuristic (goal-first color, nearest bin) will mismatch the annotation whenever multiple cubes are present at the start, creating memory errors since the annotator relies on future information the policy can't access. I'm weighing whether a consistent heuristic shared by both sides would be better, even though it might make later picks wrong on the subgoal side, since the core tension is that predictability requires memory-plus-step to determine memory, and the annotator peeking ahead violates that—though the report seems to accept this trade-off anyway. I need to trace through whether memory errors persist across steps given how the policy receives carried-in annotated memory from the previous step during evaluation.

Since the policy reads annotated arrivals reflecting the true pick order at later steps, subgoals end up correct there—only step 1 memory is wrong, meaning just one memory fault per episode instead of multiple subgoal faults, so I'll go with the annotation reading ahead while keeping the policy's heuristic consistent in form. I'm now reconciling this with round 3's refusal of the "first-named color" rule versus round 2's commitment to it, checking whether the round 3 contradiction cases (like one blue two green, green first) actually opened with a single cube at start, which would mean the arrivals rule doesn't actually contradict the earlier rounds' picks.

So the rule should apply only when multiple goal-color cubes are present at step 1—pick the single cube if there's only one, otherwise use first-named color and nearest bin ≥28px. This matches the report's "first color named in the goal, nearest the bin" language, and the memory instruction ordering at first step stays consistent with the subgoal. Removal only at pickup, retention using the 12px match, the release echo frame, and multi-append order all check out fine—now I'm examining whether the subgoal's "first entry of arrivals" logic is consistent with how the policy actually builds the arrivals list at step 1.

The main edit needed is deleting the "does not matter" sentence and adding an explicit step-1 clause, plus updating the release echo exclusion to match the new release-frame definition. I'm checking the "when placed is none" clause too, but that only applies at step 1 since later steps with no held cube fall under the pickup rule anyway, so it's fine as is. Now I need to find the exact current wording in the arrivals annotator prompt to make precise edits against it.

I'm replacing the first-step and later-step procedure text, then revising the subgoal rule to drop the last clause and add a note about step 1, and I'm reworking the release echo clause to better specify the detection threshold near the last known held-cube position.

For the episode-start rule, I'm adding the case split: with only one cube in play, grab that one; with multiple, pick by first-named color among those at least 28 px from the nearest bin. I'm also noting what stays excluded—no nearest-gripper or nearest-bin tie-breaks—and clarifying that reading ahead at step 1 is acceptable despite costing a memory fault, and that the first-named-color rule only applies to this specific multi-cube opening step, not as a general round-2 rule.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: Otherwise, including when `placed` is none, the working color is the color of the first entry of `arrivals` whose color is still short (the oldest cube of a needed color on the table); the order in which the goal names the colors does not matter.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: Otherwise, including when `placed` is none, the working color is the color of the first entry of `arrivals` whose color is still short (the oldest cube of a needed color on the table). At the first decision step, where several goal-color cubes may be present with no arrival order to read, `arrivals` as written at this step begins with the color named first in the goal, nearest the bin first, so that is where the first pick goes; at every later step the order the goal names the colors plays no part.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: a detection of the just-released color within about 12 px of where the held cube was last reported or of the gripper in the frame where the fingers opened (release echo), unless that same detection was already at the same place in the first execution frame of the step;
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: a release echo, meaning a detection of the just-released color that first appeared in or after the release frame (the first execution frame of this step with the fingers about 100% open and no held line) within about 12 px of the gripper reported there, or that moved a few px with the retreating gripper from frame to frame, excluded however far it is from the bin; a detection already at the same place in the first execution frame of the step, or matching a carried `arrivals` entry within about 12 px, is not an echo;

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is none, so pick up the cube that is first in `arrivals` among those of a needed color.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is none, so pick up the cube that is first in `arrivals` among those of a needed color: with one goal-color cube in the scene, that cube; with several, the cube of the color named first in the goal that is nearest the bin's reported center while at least about 28 px from it.

edits.modify_from: At the very first decision step (carried-in memory blank, no execution frames) list every goal-color cube in the scene, ordered by y as reported (smaller y first).
edits.modify_to: At the very first decision step (carried-in memory blank, no execution frames): if exactly one goal-color cube is in the scene, the list is that cube. If several are, the scene does not show which came first; list first the cubes of the color named first in the goal instruction, then the other goal color(s) in the order the goal names them, and within each color order by distance to the bin's reported center, nearest first, skipping any detection within about 28 px of that center. A cube of a color the goal does not name is never listed.

edits.modify_from: (1) if an execution frame shows a cube held in the gripper, remove the entry nearest the gripper position in the frame where the fingers first closed on it (within about 12 px); (2) drop any entry that has no table detection of its color within about 12 px in the scene at this decision step (the last frame); (3) append, at the end, each goal-color table detection in the last frame that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px, unless it is a bin echo (within about 28 px of the bin's reported center) or a release echo (a detection of the just-released color within about 12 px of where the held cube was last reported or of the gripper at the frame the fingers opened); (4) update each remaining entry to its last-frame position. Order is never changed except by removal and appending.
edits.modify_to: (1) PICK-UP REMOVAL, only if some execution frame of this step shows the fingers about 100% open over a table cube and a later frame of this step shows them at about 46% with a cube then reported held: remove the entry within about 12 px of the gripper in the frame where the fingers first reached 46%. If the very first execution frame already shows a cube held (fingers 46%, a held line), this is a put-into-bin step and nothing is removed, whatever entry lies near the gripper. Never remove an entry that still matches a detection of its color within about 12 px in the last frame; never stretch the 12 px test to the nearest entry. (2) RETAIN AND REFRESH: each remaining entry that has a detection of its color within about 12 px in the last frame is kept and set to that position; this match ignores the bin-echo and release-echo tests, which concern only new detections. Drop an entry with no such detection. (3) APPEND NEW: a goal-color table detection in the last frame that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px is appended unless it is a bin echo (within about 28 px of the bin's reported center) or a release echo. The release frame is the first execution frame of this step where the fingers are about 100% open with no held line; a frame with fingers 67-99% open is not it. A release echo is a detection of the just-released color that first appeared in or after the release frame within about 12 px of the gripper reported in that frame, or that has moved a few px with the retreating gripper from frame to frame; it is excluded even when far from the bin center. A detection that was already at its place in the first execution frame of the step, or that matches a carried entry, is never an echo. A detection that appears mid-step more than about 28 px from the bin center and more than about 12 px from the release point and stays put is a genuine new cube: append it. (4) When several new detections are appended, append them in the order of the execution frame in which each first appeared, earliest first, tracking each across frames within about 12 px; same-frame arrivals follow that frame's listing order. Order is otherwise never changed. Example: carried [[77, 139]], a pick-up step closing on [77, 139], with a red cube that appeared at [100, 66] several frames earlier far from bin and gripper, and two red detections within 28 px of the bin: write [[100, 66]].

edits.modify_from: At step #1 the list holds every goal-color cube in the scene, ordered by y as reported (smaller y first).
edits.modify_to: At step #1 the list holds every goal-color cube in the scene (a cube of a color the goal does not name is never listed). With one goal-color cube in the scene the list is that cube. With several, the scene gives no arrival order, so the annotator, reading the whole episode, lists first the pre-existing cubes the oracle actually picks during the episode in the order it picks them (first-picked first), and after them the never-picked cubes of a needed color ordered by distance to the bin's reported center, nearest first, skipping detections within about 28 px of that center.

edits.modify_from: At each later step: remove the entry of the cube the robot picked up during the step (the entry nearest where the fingers closed on a cube); append, at the end, every goal-color detection on the table in the scene at the decision step that matches no existing entry within about 12 px, except bin echoes (within about 28 px of the bin's reported center) and release echoes (a detection of the just-released color within about 12 px of where the held cube was last reported or of the gripper when the fingers opened); drop an entry that no longer has a detection of its color within about 12 px in the scene at the decision step; refresh each remaining entry to its position in the scene at the decision step.
edits.modify_to: At each later step, in order: (1) removal, only at a pick-up step (one whose execution frames show the fingers going from open to about 46% while the gripper is over a table cube, followed by a held line): remove the entry within about 12 px of the gripper in that closing frame. At a put-into-bin step, where the first execution frame already shows a cube held, remove nothing (the held cube's entry was already removed at its pick-up step). Never remove an entry that still has a detection of its color within about 12 px in the scene at the decision step; the 12 px test is never stretched to the nearest entry. (2) retention: an entry that has a detection of its color within about 12 px in the scene at the decision step is kept and refreshed to that position; the bin-echo and release-echo exclusions do not apply here, so an entry matching a detection near the just-released cube's last reported position or near the gripper at release is kept. An entry with no such detection is dropped. (3) appending: every goal-color detection in the scene at the decision step that matches no remaining entry within about 12 px is appended, except bin echoes (within about 28 px of the bin's reported center) and release echoes. The release frame is the first execution frame in which the fingers are about 100% open and no object line says held (a frame with fingers 67-99% open is not it). A release echo is a detection of the just-released color that first appears in or after the release frame within about 12 px of the gripper reported there, or that moves a few px along with the retreating gripper over the following frames; it is never appended however far it is from the bin center. A detection is not an echo if it matches an existing entry within about 12 px or was already at the same place in the first execution frame of the step. A goal-color detection that appears during the step more than about 28 px from the bin center and more than about 12 px from the release point and then stays put is a genuine new arrival and is appended. (4) when several detections are appended in one step, append them in the order of the execution frame in which each first appeared (earliest first), tracking each across frames within about 12 px; two that first appear in the same frame follow that frame's listing order. Example over a step in which a green cube appeared at [86, 143] in an early frame and another at [86, 95] in a later frame, with [86, 119] picked up: [[86, 143], [86, 95]].
